title: One-shot fallback arbitrator — scratch
body:
Context:
- Hypothesis: for low-latency, low-cost queries where a single-turn user prompt needs a reliable answer, we can apply a fast "one-shot" arbitration layer to pick a fallback model/variant when the primary route is expected to fail SLOs or cost budget.
- This is different from long-session QoS routing: it's per-request, decision must be fast (<15ms budget ideally), and conservative (avoid noticeable regressions).

Problem statement:
- Hosted API customers see occasional spikes where model A (highest quality) has tail latency or throttling; automatic fallback to smaller models exists but is blunt: either route to a lower model class for all requests, or never.
- Need: per-request fallback decision that considers request signals (prompt size, stop tokens, user-specified max latency), real-time capacity signals, and expected quality delta.

Goal (MVP):
- Build a lightweight "one-shot fallback arbitrator" service that, for each eligible request, returns either: PASS (use primary model) or FALLBACK_TO=<variant> with a short rationale token.
- Must integrate with smart routing layer with an opt-in header: X-Opt-In-OneShot-Fallback: true.
- Keep decision latency < 25ms 95th in steady-state.
- Telemetry: log decision, score, features used, final chosen model, whether fallback actually used (execution result).

User stories:
- As a product developer, I want short, transient fallbacks for single-turn assistant prompts so my app stays responsive during capacity spikes.
- As SRE, I want clear telemetry to validate that fallbacks reduce tail latency incidents without large regressions in correctness.
- As customer success, I want opt-in controls per-API-key and per-route so enterprise customers can disable risky fallbacks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature flag + per-API-key opt-in implemented (console + API).
- Default policy: consider fallback candidates from curated list [gpt-small, gpt-med-q4_0, gpt-compact-8bit] with conservative threshold.
- Canary rollout on 1% of traffic for 2 weeks with automatic revert if user-visible error rate increases > 1.5x baseline.
- End-to-end tests and a simulation harness using historical request traces to estimate perceived quality loss.

Design notes / approach:
- Decision model: lightweight scoring function, not full ML initially. Inputs: prompt token length, expected output tokens (client max_tokens), route latency prediction (from recent P95), API-key tier, cost-weight (client-configurable), last-minute capacity hints.
- Score = alpha * latency_risk + beta * cost_savings - gamma * estimated_quality_loss. Threshold determines fallback. Tunable via remote server config.
- Quality loss estimate: proxy by model BLEU/ROUGE delta from offline eval on short prompt slices (keep conservative multiplier).
- Side-channel: if request contains "prefer_accuracy=true" header, fallbacks disabled.

API sketch (minimal):
- Pre-routing call (sync HTTP) -> POST /v1/arbitrate { api_key, route, prompt_meta } returns { action: "pass" | "fallback", variant: null | "gpt-med-q4_0", reason: "latency-risk/high" }
- Alternatively integrated into main routing decision path to avoid extra network hop (toggle at infra).

Telemetry + metrics to collect:
- decision_rate, fallback_rate, fallback_success_rate (fallback prevented SLA breach), request_latency_by_decision, downstream_quality_regressions (tracked via sampling + eval harness), per-api-key opt-in fraction, canary safety metrics.

Experiment plan:
- Phase 0: offline simulation on 30 days of request traces; compute theoretical tail-latency reduction and estimated quality loss.
- Phase 1: internal-only canary on dev customers with per-API-key opt-in, 0.5% traffic; measure telemetry for 1 week.
- Phase 2: public canary 1% traffic, 2 weeks. If safe, ramp to configurable default on lower tiers (dev/prod non-enterprise).

Rollout controls / customer UX:
- Console toggle per-api-key, per-route.
- Two modes: conservative (prefer accuracy, fewer fallbacks) and aggressive (prefer latency/cost).
- Expose simple "fallback history" table in Console showing recent fallback events with reasons and sampled outputs.

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: invisible quality regressions for edge prompts. Mitigation: aggressive sampling + A/B evals comparing original vs fallback on production-captured prompts (with privacy redaction).
- Decision latency budget: where to host arbitrator? colocated with router vs separate service. Tradeoffs: speed vs deployment complexity.
- Can we reuse existing routing heuristics / cache of model p95 predictions instead of building new store?
- Legal / compliance: enterprise customers may require opt-out by default. Need tenant-level flags and audit logs.

Short TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Spike: implement scoring function stub in routing proxy (2d).
- [ ] Run offline sim job on 60M requests (data infra ticket INF-1342).
- [ ] Create Console mockups for per-route toggle and fallback history (ask UX: Jonah Lee).
- [ ] Draft canary run playbook and safety thresholds.

Notes to self:
- Keep default conservative; early wins are latency tail reduction with <0.5% user-visible degraded answers.
- Consider combining with prefix caching: if request hits cache, arbitrator should always PASS.
- Remember to add logs that map to billing so we can attribute cost delta to fallbacks.

References / links in my head:
- Related tickets: INF-1342 (simulation), INF-1420 (console flags); PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/278
- Slack channel: #eng-routing for quick syncs

End.
